newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's economy grows 2.2 percent, rate cuts still seen.
newsitem.headline: Spain's economy grows 2.2 percent, rate cuts still seen.

text.p: Spain's economic growth accelerated in the fourth quarter to post an overall 2.2 percent gain last year, but economists said Wednesday the rise would not threaten expected interest rate cuts this year.
Gross domestic product expanded at a 2.6 percent rate in the fourth-quarter over the year-ago quarter and at a 0.8 percent rate from the third quarter for a total 2.2 percent 1996 growth.

The government had forecast real growth of 2.3 percent for 1996 and of three percent for 1997. Although the 1996 figure was slightly beneath the government's forecast, it was a bit better than financial markets had expected.
"The data are good, a little bit better than we expected," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist at Societe Generale in Madrid.
But economists said the growth was not strong enough to prevent the Bank of Spain from further lowering interest rates.
The central bank has cut its key interest rate to a current 6 percent from 9 percent at the start of 1996 amid a sharp fall in the inflation rate and fiscal belt-tightening.
